Still, Plague Rat’s nasty, but is he really a temporal-scale threat? In the game itself, he’s a damage-dealing beast, but sending a time agent to deal with him?

Maybe in one future timeline, Plague Rat infects and controls the majority of the current heroes, using them to lay waste to the Chairman and his Conspiracy, which drove Rat underground in the first place. Chairman Pike retaliates with extreme prejudice, turning Rook City into a blighted wasteland which claims the lives of its indigenous heroes. The remaining villains such as Citizen Dawn and Baron Blade seize the opportunity to strike hard and advance their agendas, with Dawn and Blade teaming up to help repel the threat of Legacy and the Freedom Five (Six?), leading directly to Pauline Parson’s death. This, in turn, forces Paul to desperate measures, leading him to put a permanent end to Dawn, Blade, and anyone else threatening the security of his world. With no one left able to remotely threaten him, Legacy declares a new golden age for the world, enforced by him at any cost. The existing transhumans either work for Legacy or are destroyed, the reasoning being that if they are controlled or eliminated, they can’t wreak unmitigated havoc on Legacy’s world. The world’s governments, rendered effectively powerless as long as Legacy rules, begin to devise weaponized transhuman programs that will allow them to throw off the yoke of Legacy’s rule; it is one such program that gives birth to the Visionary. The tension between Legacy and the remnants of national governments reaches critical mass. Then, Legacy’s most trusted lieutenant is murdered in his sleep, which ignites the powder keg, creating the future the Visionary is so desperate to stop.

Unbeknownst to anyone, the Visionary and Chrono-Ranger are actually working toward the same goal; the Visionary sees too much of a big picture thanks to her abilities, and feels that tempus is fugiting furiously thanks to the bleeding aneurysm, while Chrono-Ranger knows that as long as Plague Rat is stopped before a certain time, then the majority of the catastrophe will be averted.

Odds are that I’m completely wrong, of course.

-CSR
